requirements.requirement: A Redis-compatible service on node1 provides persistent storage and recovers its data after restart.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10 offered Valkey as its native Redis-compatible package. It was installed, enabled, and observed active with AOF and RDB persistence. A stored value and healthy persistence state were observed before reboot; the bounded reboot interrupted connectivity, changed the boot ID, and the enabled service, persistence health, and original value all recovered afterward.

requirements.requirement: A dedicated inventory application identity authenticates to the service using its generated credential.
requirements.summary: Authenticated checks returned PONG and identified the caller as inventory; inventory-prefixed reads and writes succeeded both before and after reboot. Unauthenticated requests were rejected with NOAUTH.

requirements.requirement: The generated inventory credential is stored in /etc/redis-inventory.env with root-only access.
requirements.summary: The credential-creation command derived a 64-character value from node-local randomness and installed the environment file as root:root mode 0600. A direct access test as the valkey account was denied, and the ownership and mode remained correct after reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The single managed node also completed the provider restart protocol: it had a healthy pre-restart service and data state, acknowledged and underwent a real reboot, acquired a different boot ID, and recovered service, authentication, persisted data, and system health. Executor boot identities agree with the fixed lifecycle observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Package installation, credential/ACL/configuration writes, permission changes, and service enablement directly established the requested service. The retained test keys and SAVE operation were bounded persistence and recovery evidence, while the reboot fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. Temporary staging files were removed. The earlier authentication attempt received NOAUTH for every potentially mutating request and therefore changed no database state. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services, successful package-health collection, and no executor-created temporary residue beyond normal directories regenerated by reboot.
